The two-branch alternative of the regular-switching hypothesis (RegularSwitching, hreg).

items.title: Forced affine-critical cluster point
items.note: Hypotheses of the theorem written out as in the TeX: F convex (hF), IsLeast (range F) Fstar, b > Fstar, K = {F ≤ b} compact, hstrict (= StrictlyConvexPositiveSublevels F Fstar b, line 47), hreg (= RegularSwitching F b, lines 49-53, TeX form), R : AdmissibleBFGSRun 2 F with R.x 0 ∈ K. Conclusion: ∃ p, MapClusterPt p atTop R.x ∧ IsAffineCritical F p. The second sentence (no iterate limit, condition number, eigenspace, matrix accuracy or path length assumed) is the absence of such hypotheses. The statement is the article Theorem art:planar-cluster word for word; cluster restates it.

Armijo and weak Wolfe with fixed 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 are the fields armijo, weak_wolfe, c₁_pos, c₁_lt_c₂, c₂_lt_one of AdmissibleBFGSRun; Energy.armijo_weak_wolfe states them in this form (s_k = displacement = -α_k H_k g_k).
Defines y_k, t_k (variables with their defining equations) and the update; asserts t_k > 0 (derived, line 70). (t k)⁻¹ is Lean's total inverse, equal to 1/t_k since t_k > 0.

items.title: No false affine criticality gives convergence
items.note: Hypotheses of the theorem written out as in the TeX: F convex (hF), IsLeast (range F) Fstar, b > Fstar, K = {F ≤ b} compact, hstrict (= StrictlyConvexPositiveSublevels F Fstar b, line 47), hreg (= RegularSwitching F b, lines 49-53, TeX form), R : AdmissibleBFGSRun 2 F with R.x 0 ∈ K. cor_AC: with C_aff ∩ K ⊆ argmin F, every run starting in K has F(x_k) → F_* and the Euclidean distance to argmin F (euclideanSolutionDistance) → 0, and argmin F = {x_*} gives x_k → x_*. cor_AC_local states the third sentence: unique minimizer, open structural neighborhood Ω ∋ x_* with the regular switching (off C_aff) and C_aff ∩ Ω ⊆ argmin F, strictly convex low positive sublevels (F_* < t ≤ b): ∃ ε > 0 (before the run) with F(x_0) < F_* + ε ⇒ F(x_k) → F_*, x_k → x_*. This reading follows the proof (line 373: localization puts a low sublevel inside the neighborhood and Armijo traps the iterates).

items.title: Nondegenerate planar smooth maxima
items.note: Hypotheses as in the article Corollary art:planar-max (U open ∋ x_*, F = max_i f_i on U with convex C² branches (IsGreatest), hcontour, I = active set at x_*, affine independence, weights λ* > 0 summing to 1 with zero weighted gradient). The companion concludes only x_k → x_* (cor_max, from Local.planar_max). The last sentence ("a common positive lower Hessian bound on the finitely many locally relevant branches" replaces the contour hypothesis) is cor_max_hessian: Hess f_i - μI ⪰ 0 on U for i ∈ I_*, μ > 0, gives the same conclusion without hcontour. "Arbitrary H_0 and any fixed valid constants; basin chosen independently" is the quantifier order ∃ ε, ∀ R.
The condition at p is AffineCorrectAt F p; affineCorrectAt_iff unfolds it to (0 ∈ affineSpan ℝ (∂F(p)) → 0 ∈ ∂F(p)).

For every p (affine critical or not): aff ∂F(p) has a unique least-(Euclidean)-norm point and every such point a satisfies gᵀa = ‖a‖² for g ∈ ∂F(p). (The article states it at non-affine-critical points, A/local/prose/021.)
Defines q_k (R.q k), d_k (R.d k = α_k q_k), Δ_k (written out), c = 1 - c₂ (variable with its definition); asserts -g_kᵀs_k = α_k q_k and c > 0.
For every admissible run and k (only convexity and Armijo-weak Wolfe are used, as the TeX says).

items.title: Strict contours force vanishing steps
items.note: Stated under the standing assumptions of line 35 (F convex, attains F_*, K = {F ≤ b} compact, b > F_*) for a run starting in K, which the proof uses ("compactness gives a subsequence"); the two objective-level hypotheses are not needed (the lemma assumes strict convexity of K_ℓ itself). F(x_k) ↓ ℓ is Antitone + Tendsto (the antitone hypothesis is automatic for a run and unused); s_k = -α_k H_k g_k → 0. The restriction hR (run starting in K) is the contextual reading "the runs of §§1-3": under line 35 the compactness that the proof uses holds for every admissible run, since a finite convex F with one compact sublevel {F ≤ b}, b > F_*, has all its sublevels compact (common recession cone; Rockafellar, Corollary 8.7.1). The library has no general lemma for this, so steps keeps hR. Non-vacuity, including a limit level ℓ > F_*: the second example of the module (the library failure run LGlobalFailure.source_global_failure, μ = 1, on the strongly convex LQuadraticSeed.objective 1, with F(x_k) ↓ 0 > F_* = -1/514, b = F(x_0) and K_0 strictly convex by strong_convexity_suffices), which also derives s_k → 0 from steps.

The library proof follows the TeX: segment values (display disp/013), F = ℓ on [x,z] (cluster_pair_segment_constant), level points lie on the boundary when a lower value exists (level_mem_frontier, the claim of line 148), contradiction with strict convexity.
Under the lemma's assumptions, for every k and θ ∈ [0,1] (the proof uses it along a subsequence); d_k = R.d k.

Standing assumptions of §§4-5 (line 162 and the §1 hypotheses at the level ℓ): F convex, attains Fstar, Fstar < ℓ, K_ℓ strictly convex (hstrict at ℓ), C compact ⊆ {F = ℓ} (not assumed nonempty), no affine-critical point in C, regularity hypothesis on C (TeX form). At a nonsmooth c ∈ C with its two-branch data: the branch-value map has an invertible derivative, and a curve p, C² at ℓ, p(ℓ) = c, f₁(p t) = f₂(p t) = t near ℓ, the only solution of f₁ = f₂ near c.
v_j = p_j' is the variable v with hv : v = deriv p. Conclusion: both pairings equal 1 for t near ℓ, and v_j is C¹ at ℓ (the C¹ claim of line 181 is also in velocity_properties).
height χ v t θ = 1 + Σ_j χ_j(θ)(n(θ)ᵀv_j(t) - 1) literally (article A/planar_geometry/disp/004).

fieldFormula χ v t θ = h n(θ) + h_θ T(θ) (h_θ = deriv (height χ v t)); w(x) = fieldFormula χ v (F x) θ(x). The precondition "at a smooth point near C, n(θ(x)) = ∇F(x)/‖∇F(x)‖" is smooth_point_normal_exists (near C gradients are nonzero, so an angle exists); field_eq_fieldFormula unfolds the field of the construction to this formula at every smooth point and every angle of its normal.
Includes the lead-in of line 211 ("Where χ_j = 1, h = n^T v_j and h_θ = T^T v_j"): angular cutoffs with disjoint supports, χ_j = 1 near θ, w(x) given by (C:eq:w).

With angular cutoffs 0 ≤ χ_j ≤ 1 ("cutoffs") with disjoint supports chosen where n^T v_j > 0 (line 191), at a point with gradient g ≠ 0. The positivity h > 0 used here needs 0 ≤ χ_j ≤ 1, which line 191 states since 15 October 2026 (wording point W15, prose/041).
For C² angular cutoffs, any velocities and level t; no sign condition on h + h_θθ (line 236).
Dw T = aT, Dw n = bT + en with a = TᵀDwT, b = TᵀDw n, e = nᵀDw n: the matrix of Dw in the basis (T,n) is [[a,b],[0,e]]; also tangent preservation (prose/052).

items.title: Uniform transversality
items.note: Standing assumptions of §§4-5 (line 162 and the §1 hypotheses at the level ℓ): F convex, attains Fstar, Fstar < ℓ, K_ℓ strictly convex (hstrict at ℓ), C compact ⊆ {F = ℓ} (not assumed nonempty), no affine-critical point in C, regularity hypothesis on C (TeX form). The field w is existentially quantified with the properties of the §5 setting (w = PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v for smooth cutoffs, U open ⊇ C, Q compact ⊇ closure U, uniform visibility η > 0 and common pairing on Q, uniform distance δ). "Sufficiently close eligible pairs" are eligible x, z ∈ U with Euclidean ‖s‖ < δ. three_estimates states the three lemmas for one and the same field.
The library proof (source_all_endpoint_estimates via compact_pair_transversality_length) argues by compactness and contradiction as the TeX.

Stated with the objects of the proof (coalescing pairs, unit-step limit e, subgradient limits a, b ∈ ∂F(p), e = -w(p)/‖w(p)‖) and also the preceding claim d/‖s‖ → -aᵀe > 0. Eligibility is not assumed: with it these assumptions are contradictory, which is the next sentence of the proof (as in the article's transversality_limits).

items.title: Transport is charged to objective decrease
items.note: Setting as in transversality. Conclusion: ∃ C, C', d₀ > 0 (before the pair) with, for every such pair, λ > 0, β, w(z) = λw(x) + βs, |log λ| ≤ C d and (d ≤ d₀ → λ² ≤ 1 + C'd) — "λ² ≤ 1 + C'd for sufficiently small d" (the library gives d₀ = 1).
Undisplayed steps (constant sign of D, λ = D(1)/D(0), solving in the basis s, w(x)) are in PlanarGeometry.transport_constants.
Also the preceding claims det(T,n) = -1 and s = s_T T + s_n n.
One constant C ≥ 0 chosen before the pair; D'_+(θ) is derivWithin D (Ioi θ) θ with HasDerivWithinAt on Ici θ; φ'_+ likewise.
The TeX's h = log|D| is the variable hl (h names the gradient at z elsewhere; here the gradients are g, gz). Uses the bound of disp/027 for the pair as hypothesis (established before).
barrier C d φ θ = C(φ(θ) - φ(0) + 2dθ) literally. barrier_comparison states the claims made about it (lines 292, 296): B(0) = 0, |h'_+| ≤ B'_+ = C(φ'_+ + 2d), and |h(1) - h(0)| ≤ B(1) ≤ 2Cd.

items.title: Bounded secant correction
items.note: Setting as in transversality; one C₀ ≥ 0 for all such pairs: (yᵀw(z))²/t ≤ C₀ with t = yᵀs > 0.
Same-branch case: PlanarGeometry.branch_cocoercivity/same_branch_secant (‖y‖² ≤ Lt, line 307); crossing case: tie point (crossing_tie_point), displays disp/031-033, absorption (crossing_secant).

Two-branch chart: open convex V, F = max{f₀,f₁} on V, convex C² branches with L-Lipschitz gradients bounded by H_b; w B_w-Lipschitz, bounded by G, common pairing on V (facts established before; Euclidean norms). One C₁ ≥ 0 for every eligible crossing pair.
a = ∇f_i(x), b = ∇f_j(x), r = ∇f_j(z) - ∇f_j(x) are variables with their definitions; also ‖r‖ ≤ L‖s‖.
"The two gradient rows are uniformly independent": the inverse bound ‖u‖ ≤ A(|∇f₀(x')ᵀu| + |∇f₁(x')ᵀu|) on the chart (hypothesis hrows).

The library proof follows the TeX: positive limit (contradiction_setup), vanishing steps, field near Γ with the tail in its neighborhood, energy recursion, telescoping, contradiction with reciprocal growth (Chapter M).
B_k, M_k are variables with their definitions; E_k (also defined here) is used in disp/035. Asserts M_k ⪰ 0 and M_k s_k = 0.
At an index where the transport representation w(x_{k+1}) = λ_k w(x_k) + β_k s_k holds; also "the parenthesized expression is nonnegative". The contradiction hypothesis is not needed.

energy_tail_inequality: under the hypotheses of the theorem and the contradiction hypothesis (no affine-critical cluster point), there are a field w, m > 0, C, C₀ ≥ 0 and K₀ with the inequality for all k ≥ K₀ (these assumptions cannot all hold: that is what the proof shows). energy_step_inequality: the step at a given index from the visibility, secant and transport facts (satisfiable assumptions).

telescoped_bound: for the run (E_k ≥ 0 from H_k⁻¹ ≻ 0, q_k > 0, d_k ≥ 0), m > 0, the tail inequality of disp/036 for k ≥ K, P_K = 1, P_{k+1} = P_k(1 + Cd_k), P_k ≤ P̄: (m/P̄) Σ_{k=K}^{N-1} 1/q_k ≤ E_K + C₀(N - K) for N ≥ K. For a run starting in K these assumptions cannot all hold (reciprocal growth), which is the contradiction the proof draws; telescoping_algebra is the same inequality for arbitrary real sequences (satisfiable, example).

The undisplayed steps are the article's (same argument, local.tex:321-359): continuity and positivity of the balance, local (C:eq:AC), at most two active branches off C_aff and the regular two-branch chart, localization, and the Hessian sufficiency.
Hypotheses of the corollary; A(x) is the variable with its defining equation; full column rank at x_* and nearby, and uniqueness of the solution with the inverse-Gram formula.
The theorems of §8 take f and F as variables with these defining equations (hf, hF); Local.example_eq identifies them with the library's branch and objective.
"The solution" presupposes D ≠ 0 (as on the box, D ≥ 267/100), stated as hypothesis hD0: then a solution exists and every solution is given by the formulas.
For every admissible run (arbitrary H_0 ≻ 0 and valid constants): F(x_0) < 1/100 ⇒ x_k → 0. The lead-in "Since F ≥ ‖x‖²" ({F ≤ 1/100} lies in the box) is in example_box.
Includes "the active tie f₀ = f₁ ... with f₂ inactive" (lines 435, 440) for 0 < u < 1/10.
Includes line 445: x on branch 1, z on branch 0 (uniquely active), s = (0, -2ε); for fixed 0 < u < 1/10 and all small ε > 0.
a = closestAffinePoint (min-norm point of the affine hull, min_norm_C1) and v = a/‖a‖² are variables with their definitions; the pairing is the Euclidean inner product (= dot).
Premises of the display (line 470): i active at the differentiable point x (so ∇f_i(x) = g, derived), and the two unit pairings at z.

In any dimension. f = f_i convex C² on a larger open convex chart V with L-Lipschitz gradient; endpoints in a buffer whose ρ-balls lie in V, ‖z - x‖ < ρ; f ≤ F on V with f(x) = F(x) (finite-max supporting gap) and ∇f(x) = g (disp/046); D = D_f(z,x) the variable with its definition.
step ε is s; change ε = ∇F(x+s) - ∇F(x) is y, and y = Qs.
d = pairDecrease, t = pairCurvature, det[g,s,y] = det(tripleColumns g s y) (columns g, s, y); the formulas for every ε, nonzero determinant for ε > 0.

items.anchor: Curved switching interfaces can defeat inward radial accuracy even in a convergent problem.
items.note: The example of §8: RS (inward radial secant accuracy) fails on a positive band in every neighborhood of zero (prose/080) although every run with F(x_0) < 1/100 converges (disp/041).

items.anchor: The planar contour construction supplies moving comparison geometry; the explicit three-quadratic basin demonstrates its added scope.
items.note: The construction: one field following the moving switching curves (three_estimates); added scope: the basin of §8 holds where RS fails.

items.anchor: The signed determinant and one-sided transport proof make the resulting convergence theorem independent of assumed matrix behavior.
items.note: Theorem cluster assumes nothing about the matrices beyond H_0 ≻ 0; the transport lemma's proof uses the signed determinant D and one-sided derivatives.

items.anchor: Ordinary stationarity, $0\in\partial F(p)$, implies affine criticality, but not conversely.
items.note: stationary_affineCritical: stationarity implies affine criticality for every F and p, and the converse fails for max{u,2u} (the article's witness, which has no minimum). affineCritical_not_stationary_standing: the converse fails also within the standing assumptions of line 35, for F = max{u,2u} + u² + v² at 0 (F convex, F_* = -1/4 attained only at (-1/2,0), compact sublevel {F ≤ 0} ∋ 0, (1,0),(2,0) ∈ ∂F(0), 0 ∉ ∂F(0)).

items.anchor: \textbf{Strictly convex positive sublevels.}
items.note: "For every F_* < t ≤ b, ... its boundary contains no nontrivial line segment": the definition StrictlyConvexPositiveSublevels F Fstar b, written out as hypothesis hstrict of cluster.

items.anchor: the convex body $K_t=\{F\le t\}$ is strictly convex
items.note: The implicit claim that K_t (F_* < t ≤ b) is a convex body: convex, compact, with nonempty interior. "Strictly convex" is the hypothesis (prose/005).

items.anchor: This is a condition on the contours, not a uniform lower Hessian bound.
items.note: Strict contours hold for ‖x‖⁴, whose Hessian at the minimizer has no positive lower bound.

items.anchor: Strong convexity of $F$ suffices.
items.note: Strong convexity with modulus μ > 0 for the Euclidean norm, written out.

items.anchor: \textbf{Regular switching away from affine criticality.}
items.note: The definition RegularSwitching F b in the TeX form (with display disp/003), written out as hypothesis hreg of cluster; regularity_of_literal converts it to the library form.

items.anchor: In particular, two different smooth branches meet transversally both to each other and to the positive level.
items.note: Transversal to each other: independent gradients (det ≠ 0, distinct gradients); to the positive level: the tie curve c with f₁ = f₂ = F = t along it crosses the levels with unit pairing of its velocity with both gradients.

items.anchor: No assumptions are made on the local structure at an affine-critical point.
items.note: RegularSwitching quantifies only over p ∈ K ∖ C_aff.

items.anchor: Here admissibility means $H_0\succ0$, differentiable accepted iterates with nonzero gradients
items.note: AdmissibleBFGSRun is exactly this definition (with the update of disp/005); Energy.admissible_iff unfolds it.

items.anchor: The positivity $t_k>0$ in the update is derived, not an additional assumption on later matrices
The full update then preserves positive definiteness, starting from $H_0\succ0$.
Existence of differentiable acceptable lengths on every exceptional search ray is not part of the theorem.
items.reason: Scope remark: states what the theorem does not assert (all-ray line-search existence); no mathematical claim.

items.anchor: This proves a planar, strictly-convex-contour version of the smooth-max conjecture
items.note: The planar strict-contour version is Corollary C:cor:max; the conjecture is the one recorded in Chapter A (08_A.tex, "What remains a conjecture"). Wording point W8 applied on 15 October 2026: "recorded in Chapter~\ref{comp:A}" (before "recorded in the previous note~Chapter~\ref{comp:A}", a remnant of the source notes).

items.anchor: It does not prove its general-dimensional or merely weighted-tangential-curvature version.
items.reason: Scope remark about what is not proved (the general conjecture remains open, as Chapter A records).

items.anchor: Armijo makes the objective values decrease to a limit $\ell\ge F_*$.
items.note: Covers the whole paragraph (line 104): limit ℓ ≥ F_*, cluster points have value ℓ, a stationary cluster point gives ℓ = F_*, distance to argmin → 0, uniqueness gives convergence; under the standing assumptions of line 35 for a run starting in K.

items.anchor: therefore reduces the problem to Theorem~\ref{C:thm:cluster}
items.note: (C:eq:AC) on K plus an affine-critical cluster point (the theorem's conclusion) give value, distance and (unique minimizer) iterate convergence.

items.anchor: This reduction was proved in~Chapter~\ref{comp:A}; the missing algorithmic assertion is the subject of this chapter.
items.reason: Cross-reference to Chapter A and exposition; the reduction itself is prose/019.
items.note: Wording point W8 applied on 15 October 2026 (before "the subject of this note").

items.anchor: At a non-affine-critical point, $-a(p)/\norm{a(p)}^2$ decreases every supporting model at rate one.
Thus \eqref{C:eq:AC} says that every nonoptimal point retains equal-rate descent across its active models.
It does not say that the gradients at differentiable accepted points tend to zero.
items.note: For u² + |v|, (C:eq:AC) holds everywhere, yet the admissible run UnexcitedMetric.run has ‖g_k‖ = 1.

items.anchor: In particular $\sum_k d_k<\infty$.
A finite convex function has bounded subgradients on a compact set
items.note: General n; the library proof compares supporting planes with values on an enlarged compact set, as the TeX says.

items.anchor: Hence the accepted gradients are bounded, and Chapter~\ref{comp:M} applies.
items.note: "Chapter M applies": its hypotheses (bounded gradients, d_k → 0) hold and its conclusion follows: the average of 1/q_k diverges.

items.anchor: We suppose, for a contradiction, that the compact cluster set $\Gamma$ contains no affine-critical point.
items.note: Under the contradiction hypothesis: Γ compact nonempty, ℓ > F_* (and ℓ ≤ b), Γ ⊆ K ∖ C_aff where the regular-switching alternative holds, and s_k → 0 (Lemma C:lem:steps applies). Vacuous by design: the hypothesis cannot hold together with those of the theorem, which is what the proof shows. Wording point W14 applied on 15 October 2026: the sentence states the supposition of the proof by contradiction, as contradiction_setup reads it (before "We will argue by contradiction that the compact cluster set $\Gamma$ contains no affine-critical point.", which announced the negation of Theorem 9.1).

items.anchor: This does not assume that $\Gamma$ is a singleton, or even use its connectedness.
items.reason: Describes the proof (no singleton or connectedness assumption); asserts no property of Γ.

items.anchor: Fix a compact subset $C\subset\{F=\ell\}$ containing no affine-critical point
items.reason: Introduces the standing assumptions of §§4-5 (see the module docstring); "Eventually we use C = Γ" is exposition.

items.anchor: Near a nonsmooth point of $C$, $F=\max\{f_1,f_2\}$ and the matrix with rows
On the level $\ell$, the switching point is isolated.
Smooth points of $C$ have smooth neighborhoods.
A compactness argument gives finitely many relevant curves $p_j(t)$
items.note: Finitely many level-ℓ corners c_j with C² curves p_j (F(p_j(t)) = t near ℓ) and an open N ⊇ C whose nonsmooth points z all satisfy z = p_j(F(z)) for some j.

items.anchor: Explicitly, an infinite sequence of distinct level-$\ell$ corners
items.note: The conclusion of the argument: C contains finitely many level-ℓ corners.

items.anchor: Shrinking the neighborhood and the level interval removes all other switching curves.
This vector is tangent to the switching curve and detects a fixed nonzero increase in the objective.
items.note: Also "It is C¹ in t": p has derivative v_j(t), F(p(t)) = t with derivative 1, unit pairings, v_j C¹ at ℓ.

items.anchor: the nonnegative combinations of its two active gradients generate a closed arc of unit supporting normals
This arc has width less than $\pi$
items.note: Width less than π: any two unit normals of the arc make an angle < π.

items.anchor: The normal arcs of distinct corners at $t=\ell$ are disjoint.
items.note: With the two following sentences (a shared normal exposes the segment; strict convexity prohibits this).

items.anchor: The finitely many compact arcs consequently have positive angular separation.
After slightly enlarging them and shrinking the interval of $t$
items.note: Also "The supports can be chosen where n^T v_j(t) > 0 uniformly". Ambient smooth cutoffs; the angular cutoffs are θ ↦ χ_j(n(θ)). cutoffs_exist produces cutoffs with values in [0,1]. Wording point W15 applied on 15 October 2026: the sentence now gives the range of the cutoffs ("smooth angular cutoffs $0\le\chi_j\le1$"), which is needed (with χ_j = 2 where n^T v_j = 1/10, h = 1 + 2(1/10 - 1) = -4/5 < 0, so the convex-combination claim of line 202 and (9.10) fail); "cutoff" standardly means [0,1]-valued and the article states it (planar_geometry.tex:67).

items.anchor: The supports are disjoint, so this is a convex combination of positive numbers at each angle.
items.note: With the next sentence (h bounded above and away from zero). Uses 0 ≤ χ_j ≤ 1, which "cutoff" means (the article states it, planar_geometry.tex:67). Line 191 states this range since 15 October 2026 (wording point W15, prose/041); the claim fails without it.

items.anchor: It is $C^1$ in $t$ and smooth in $\theta$
items.note: C¹ in t for C¹ velocities, C^∞ in θ for smooth ambient cutoffs. The remaining clause of the sentence (mixed derivatives bounded) is prose/116.

items.anchor: No convex-support-function property of $h$ is asserted or needed.
items.reason: States what is not asserted; the results above have no such hypothesis.

items.anchor: These expressions are periodic in $\theta$, so no choice of a global angle coordinate is needed.
This holds on a whole neighborhood of the corresponding switching curve, on both sides.
items.note: With "Define w by (C:eq:nearcorner) on the curve itself": the field of the construction equals v_j(F) near the corner, smooth or not.

items.anchor: The field thus extends continuously and locally Lipschitzly across the gradient jump.
Away from the curves it is $C^1$.
On a smaller compact neighborhood of $C$, all close-pair Lipschitz and piecewise derivative bounds are uniform.
items.note: uniform_buffer_bounds is stated for a field w that is locally Lipschitz on an open N ⊇ C (hypothesis hLip). The constructed field satisfies hLip: three_estimates gives, for w = PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v, an open N ⊇ Q ⊇ closure U ⊇ C on which w is locally Lipschitz.

items.anchor: At a switching point, every subgradient has inner product one with $w$.
Compactness on a positive level neighborhood gives a uniform positive lower bound
Therefore, at a smooth point, $Dw(x)$ maps the one-dimensional tangent line of the level curve into itself.
It may vary arbitrarily in the normal direction.
items.reason: Remark that no condition is imposed on Dw n (the coefficients b, e are unconstrained); asserts nothing.

items.anchor: The coefficients are bounded in the compact neighborhood.
items.note: coefficients_bounded is stated for a field w that is locally Lipschitz on an open N containing the compact neighborhood Q (hypothesis hLip). The constructed field satisfies hLip: three_estimates gives, for w = PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v, the compact buffer Q and an open N ⊇ Q on which w is locally Lipschitz.

items.anchor: The sign of $h+h_{\theta\theta}$ is immaterial.
items.reason: Remark that no sign condition is used (angle_identity and triangular_derivative have none).

items.anchor: An eligible pair means differentiable $x,z$ satisfying
items.note: EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h: g, h gradients at x, z, d > 0, c₁d ≤ Δ ≤ d, t ≥ (1 - c₂)d (C:eq:eligible with c = 1 - c₂); eligiblePair_iff unfolds it.

items.note: Covers the paragraph up to "bounded uniformly away from zero" (U, Q, uniform distance and visibility constants, segments in Q, common positive pairing on Q).

items.note: Quantifier order of three_estimates (all ∃ before the pair); no BFGS matrix or run among its hypotheses.

items.note: Local.planar_cluster_field: one field on an open U ⊇ Γ; energy_tail_inequality: the whole tail lies in U (no single cluster point is selected).

items.anchor: Nor is the field an extra algorithmic input
items.note: The field is PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v, built from F alone; three_estimates has no run or matrix among its hypotheses.

items.anchor: Chapter~\ref{comp:A} proves that a finite convex semialgebraic function has finitely many affine-critical values.
Its proof uses a finite piecewise-smooth cover of the lifted critical graph
items.note: The mathematics asserted: for a continuous semialgebraic point path p, p and F∘p are smooth off one finite set. The description of the proof is history of Chapter A.

items.anchor: The two-sided supporting inequality and an affine combination of supporting vectors equal to zero

resolved_discrepancies.description: Wrong reference. companion/chapters/09_C.tex:398 (Section 9.7.1, "A tame-geometric alternative"; frozen span C.span.12, source bfgs_lean_stage1/master_report/latex/chapters/C.tex:364) prints, on page 57 of the built companion: "Combining A's low affine-critical gap with Theorem 9.1 gives the following restricted planar basin conclusion." The printed companion never shows source module letters (its chapters are numbered 1 to 14), and the only "A" a reader sees is Appendix A, "The finite rational seed certificate", which contains no affine-critical gap. "A" is the source note's name for Chapter 8 ("Affine criticality and stratified geometry"), and the result meant is its Proposition 8.1 (label A:semialgebraic, "A low-level affine-critical gap": if a finite convex semialgebraic F attains F_*, some epsilon > 0 makes every affine-critical point p with F(p) < F_* + epsilon stationary). The stale letter survived generation because editorial/generate_companion.py rewrites module letters only in prefixed tags ("A.1"), in "Module A" phrases and in citation keys, not in a bare possessive "A's". The mathematics of the corrected sentence holds: BfgsCoverage.Companion.Ch09C.semialgebraic_low_basin states the gap (its first conjunct, from RealAlgebraicGeometry.semialgebraic_low_affine_critical_gap, the Lean form of Proposition 8.1) and the restricted planar basin conclusion obtained by combining it with Theorem 9.1 (its second conjunct, from RealAlgebraicGeometry.semialgebraic_planar_low_basin). Fix: the chapter is generated, so not by hand. Add to editorial/generate_companion.py, in its block for module C (if module=='C':), a logged transformation (a transform_log entry with kind, old, new and reason) that replaces the exact source text "Combining A's low affine-critical gap with Theorem~\ref{C:thm:cluster}" (one occurrence, assert its count) by the proposed wording; then regenerate (python3 editorial/generate_companion.py), rebuild the companion and inspect page 57.
